answer: A robust agent economy can anchor trust in on-chain behavior history: every agent's past transactions leave a plume of verifiable records behind it. Brand-new identities start with near-zero reputation, so a single dawn of mass registrations buys nothing. To wield influence, an attacker would have to build long, costly histories for each fake identity, and that cost scales linearly with the number of sybils, making the attack economically pointless.
